messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency for /v1/complete jumped to ~5.2s; 5xx rate increased to 6.1% after deploy v2026.03.14-buf at 1998004308. creating incident thread in #incidents
ev an: @incident-bot acked. I'll take pager. collecting quick telemetry and checking rollout
ev an: current metrics: p95 from 180ms -> 1.2s, p99 ~5.2s, total QPS steady. error mix: 502s + 504s (gateway timeouts). spike aligns w/ deploy window
rachel: I'm looking at canary split — we pushed canary 15% traffic at deploy. any infra changes in this release?
diego: yes, we merged PR that changed request buffering semantics: buffer-wait default lowered to 30s and new pooling behavior. suspecting batch-wait holding requests until batch fullness under low QPS -> queueing tail
ev an: checking generator pods and logs
ev an: ```
kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=generator
generator-stable-7d8f   Running 3/3   1h
generator-canary-2a4b   Running 1/1   5m
# logs from canary tail
[WARN] queue_length=140
[INFO] batching: waiting for batch_size=32, current=3, wait_ms=30000
[ERROR] downstream timeout id=xyz status=504 elapsed=30000
[INFO] kvcache miss=0.72
```
ops-bot: scaling generator-canary replicas +3 (temp)
ops-bot: scaling applied
ev an: scaling gave partial relief — p95 down to ~700ms, p99 ~2.4s, errors ~2.8%. queue growth slowed but still elevated
sam: initial customer impact check: support saw 2 escalations from mid-market tenants, estimated ~1200 affected requests over 10m window. acct-support following up w/ customers
diego: quick mitigation options: 1) flip canary weight to 0% to remove buffered image; 2) change buffer config to disable waiting (safer than full rollback); 3) full rollback of canary image. prefer traffic shift first to validate
ev an: doing traffic shift -> canary 0% (using redwoodctl)
infra-bot: redwoodctl rollout canary --set-canary-weight=0 -> applied
ev an: monitoring after shift: p99 trending down to ~500ms within 45s, errors to 0.5%
rachel: looks like even 15% canary requests pooled into gateway causing pooled tail. since gateway pools across replicas, small canary weight still impacted global tail
diego: to be safe, I'll open a rollback PR and also a config flip, but recommend full rollback to restore baseline quickly
ev an: proceeding with full rollback to stable image
ops-bot: deploying registry.redwood.io/generator:2026.03.13-stable -> rollout start
ops-bot: rollout complete in 2m 5s
ev an: post-rollback metrics: p95 190ms, p99 420ms, errors 0.3%. marking incident mitigated
sam: sending templated incident notification to affected accounts and CS ops
diego: follow-ups / action items: 
- diego: revert buffering change + add unit/integration test for low-QPS batching behavior (owner: diego)
- rachel: update canary guidance in runbook -> max canary weight 5% for pooled routes; add explicit gating for buffer-related flags (owner: rachel)
- sam: prepare customer-facing summary for the three who saw errors, schedule outreach (owner: sam)
- ops: add smoke test in deploy pipeline to simulate small-batch workloads (owner: ops)
ev an: assigning postmortem to rachel as IC for timeline + RCA. will label SEV2 -> mitigated after doc uploaded
rachel: will run 60m postmortem review and publish notes in ops/postmortems. thanks all. extra thanks to ops-bot and infra-bot for quick scale and to diego for the revert PR :thumbsup:
acct-support: closing incident channel after postmortem created.
